page.layout: One page of text, single column, with running head above and catchword at lower right. Two poem headings, each followed by verse stanzas. No margin notes.

main_text.head: IN EIVSDEM LIBRI carmen, quod sic incipit, Ne metuas prodire, liber.
main_text.p: QVŪ prodire tuus liber hic metuebat in auras, Quàm Domino sapuit plus liber ipse suo! Conscius obscurum genus, indoctosque[?] penates, Sciunt & esse illum nil nisi causidicum.
Hinc veritus scombros, neu portaretur Ilerdam, His Dominum tandem vocibus alloquitur.
O here, quis furor hic, quæ nunc te insania vexat? Indoctus docti iudicis ora time.
Exercere foro lites tua cura, quid ultra Tendis? ridiculus cur aliena doces?
Talia Marloreus secure sic reddidit ore: I bone, sum doctus: sic placet, ito liber.
main_text.head: IN POETAM QVI MIRIFICOS VERSVS SVBINDE FACIT.
main_text.p: Dum stas, dum recubas, coponis, equesque pedesque Græca, latina, uno carmina multa die.
Et magè quod miramur acumē idē omnibus vsq; est, Nullàque signantur de meliore nota.
Nonnunquam magnus quum dormitarit Homerus, Nec sibi sit similis doctus vbique Maro:

page.notes: The two-line heading "MIRI-/ficos" is one word, MIRIFICOS. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. The printed "fimilis", "fit", "fubinde" and "indoctofque" use an f-like long s; they were read as s and "indoctosque" is marked [?] because the abbreviation or ligature is unclear. "Græca" is read from a ligature and may be slightly off. "Marloreus" is copied as printed. "His" at lower right is the catchword. No margin notes or running-head number are printed.
